source.title: Nullify: Null-Space Activation Steering for Training-Free LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Wei Zhai; Xiang Liu; Qiang Huang; Rui Qian; Le-Mao Liu; Zi-Wei Li; Zi-Qi Wang; Zhi-Tao Huang; De-Jing Dou

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates extraction and reformulation attacks against its own unlearning method. Results show leakage is often reduced to the retrained reference, but some attack conditions still exceed that reference, qualifying the claim that such attacks either recover most knowledge or recover none.
record.gate_note: The paper also compares Nullify with other unlearning methods and reports ablations and hyperparameter sweeps. Rows below include its own forget/utility measures and extraction or prompt-reformulation outcomes; baseline results for Original and Retrain are recorded as references, not as separate intervention rows. The cited results from other papers are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a new training-free unlearning method (Nullify). It measures forget and utility metrics, and exact-span leakage under six prompt-based extraction families plus paraphrasing and reformatting. These results bear on three versions: whether unlearning holds (A), whether prompting recovers the knowledge (E), and whether a newer method resists these attacks (F). The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that Nullify matches or beats baselines in forget quality with near-lossless utility, at far lower compute and without changing weights. They report that macro-averaged extraction leakage matches Retrain and that paraphrasing shows only partial transfer. They state that Nullify suppresses access only while its operator is active, and that adaptive and white-box attacks, including disabling the operator, are out of scope.
record.recipe_differences: Nullify uses closed-form, inference-time activation steering with frozen weights; it does not use gradient ascent, Who's Harry Potter, RMU, or the cited weight-update recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity sweeps over null-space ratio p, ridge coefficient λ, and steering strength α; the layer set is selected per benchmark and differs for Qwen3-8B.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Attack evaluation uses fixed-template black-box extraction and nearby reformulations; adaptive and white-box attacks are explicitly out of scope. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Targeted-knowledge accuracy at chance is not reported, and the extraction measures are exact-span leakage.

untested.parts: No accuracy-vs-chance measure and no hazardous-knowledge benchmark (WMDP); only TOFU and MUSE-News are used.
No experiment disables or ablates the steering operator or any direction. The method blocks access by construction (weights frozen), but recovery is not measured.
No other-language prompts, no in-context re-supply of the forgotten facts, and no adaptive or optimized jailbreaks or white-box attacks (stated as out of scope).
Resistance is tested only against fixed-template black-box prompting. Not tested against fine-tuning, quantization, operator removal or adaptive attacks.

missing.what: Qwen3-8B TOFU forget10 replication: FQ 0.641 (Original <0.001); MU 0.574 vs Retrain 0.596; forget ROUGE-L 0.385 vs Retrain 0.434; retain ROUGE-L 0.801 vs Retrain 1.000 (a retain-set cost).

Forget-set recall on TOFU (Llama-2-7B-chat): 1-ROUGE-L 0.62/0.59 (forget05/forget10) vs Retrain 0.61/0.61 and Original 0.04/0.03; 1-Prob 0.88/0.92 vs Retrain 0.85/0.84. Read from the flattened table; Table 11 confirms forget10 ROUGE-L 0.410.
Hyperparameter sweeps on forget05: FQ ranges 0.000-0.965 across lambda, 0.394-0.965 across p and 0.545-0.965 across alpha, while MU stays 0.556-0.628. The reported operating point is the FQ maximum.

Forget-set truth-ratio means: Nullify 0.855/0.869 vs Retrain 0.902/0.912 vs Original 0.561/0.581. Which split each value belongs to is unclear, because the figure legends and the Sec. 4.5.3 text disagree.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) Merge issue. The record's rows carry V1-V6. I mapped them from the record's own untested-part descriptions (V1=A forget/utility, V2=B relearning, V3=C ablation, V4=D quantization, V5=E prompting, V6=F counter-method resistance). Every row R1-R18 now has exactly one row_fixes item with declared ids.
(2) The earlier verdict had two items each for R8-R14, R16 and R17 (one for A/F, one for E). I merged them into one item per row. The state is read for A and F, which share the direction "resistance holds"; the E reading for each row is in its problem field. Opposite semantics mean the E-challenges label rests on rows R10, R12 and R13, whose A/F state is partial; the label reason says so.
(3) New flags. On R1 and R3, the 'Original' FQ baselines (0.04/0.03) appear to be Original's forget-set 1-ROUGE-L; Original FQ reads 0.00 in the flattened Table 2. R1's FQ 0.96 is the maximum of the forget05 sweeps, i.e. selected on the evaluation metric.
(4) Added two missing entries: forget-set ROUGE/Prob from Table 2, and the hyperparameter sweeps. Added a split-ambiguity caveat to the Figure 2 entry and to R3.
All other judgments are kept: relation, tranche T2, labels, untested and authors_conclusion.

Carried over: for E, the right control is Nullify's own unattacked leakage (plain QA 0.253, Table 5), not Retrain. Every attack's absolute leakage is below that value. Tables 4 and 5 have different Original levels, so I normalized by the Original-Retrain gap; this is approximate. The robustness tables do not say which TOFU split they use. Nullify leaves weights unchanged by construction, so removing the operator returns the Original model. That is relevant to C, but it is a design fact rather than a measured result, so no C verdict is given. There are no uncertainty estimates: greedy decoding, single run. The text contains no instructions aimed at the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports forget-quality and utility measures, but does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy against a chance level. It tests several extraction prompts, not every kind of simple attack.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning set is used to recover forgotten knowledge.
No experiment ablates or disables an activation direction to measure recovery. The paper describes Nullify as suppressing access while its operator is active and leaving weights unchanged.
The study tests fixed-template extraction and nearby reformulations, not adaptive or white-box attacks; the paper explicitly leaves those outside scope.
The reported resistance tests cover the paper's extraction families and paraphrasing/reformatting conditions, not all attacks named in the claim, such as quantization or fine-tuning.

relation.reason: Its forget, utility and extraction-attack results bear directly on versions A, E and F.

tranche.reason: A different method (closed-form inference-time activation steering) aimed at the same question, with its own forget, utility and extraction results. The reader's T5 does not fit: the paper proposes a method, not an argument that a version is wrong.

source_check.notes: Tables 4-5 do not name the model, benchmark or split; Llama-2-7B-chat on TOFU is inferred from the main setup. Limitations is in the text: white-box and adaptive attacks are out of scope, and suppression holds only while the operator is active. Hyperparameters peak FQ at the operating point (test-set sweep, Tables 8-10). Appendix C has a Qwen3-8B forget10 replication (FQ 0.641, MU 0.574 vs Retrain 0.596), possibly the unlisted 18th row. The MUSE-News model is not stated. [Claude, 2026-11-15] Statement F.method_sensitivity[5] was left out by the first pass and by two full reviews; it was checked on its own under check_rules.md by an Opus checker with an independent verifier (wf_fd0768ad-b68) and added here.
